correctness.rationale: For every admissible full-row-rank matrix, Gershgorin bounds its Gram spectrum in [1-delta,1+delta]. SVD/nuclear duality gives the exact efficiency m/(sqrt(lambda1)sum_i sqrt(lambdai)); Cauchy--Schwarz at fixed trace and a one-variable critical point yield the global minimax. Positive equicorrelation matrices attain the lower bound; signed equicorrelation matrices attain the extremal polar-gap branches or approach a positive-definite singular limit. A self-contained verifier cross-checked 10699 finite rational and SVD identities. The proof is analytic, and finite checks are not universal proof.

originality.rationale: The original RMNP source defines the observed row statistic without the exact uniform sharp alignment frontier; its follow-up work gives diagonal-expectation heuristics, while NorMuon studies a different order of normalization. Searches found no implication providing the joint minimax efficiency and exact operator deviation over positive-definite unit-diagonal Grams with fixed minimum ratio. This is a best-knowledge originality judgment, not a priority certification. An inspected 2025 framework provides both separate linear minimization oracles but not this sharp constrained comparison.
residual_risks: An earlier general sharp eigenvalue/nuclear-to-spectral-ratio matrix optimization theorem could subsume the constrained formula under Gram diagonal and average absolute off-diagonal constraints; none was identified.

value.rationale: The motivating numerical optimizer actually reports the minimum diagonal-to-mean-off-diagonal Gram ratio and treats large values as favorable; the exact minimax shows that the correct dimension-scaled diagnostic is R/m, not simply R>1 or even R diverging. It supplies sharp phase transitions and attainable worst-case matrices for spectral-budget calibration. This is a concrete design/interpretation criterion, not an arbitrary finite slice, and no optimizer convergence theorem is inferred.
